h1: Mobile Home Leveling Cost: 2026 Prices for Ocala and Marion County
heroSub: Real numbers, not a sales pitch. Most releveling jobs in our area land between $450 and $1,500, and every job starts with a free written estimate.
introHtml:
If you're pricing out mobile home leveling, here's the honest answer: most homeowners in Ocala and Marion County pay between $450 and $1,500 for a full relevel. A singlewide sits at the low end, a doublewide at the high end, and a single sinking corner can often be fixed for $300 to $600. The exact number comes down to your home's size, how far it's settled, and what we find under there.

This guide breaks down every price we quote, from a $150 inspection to a full tie-down and anchor package. We put our numbers in writing before any work starts, so you can compare us against anyone else in town. If you'd rather just talk it through, call (352) 247-3105 and we'll give you a ballpark over the phone.

sections.heading: What Drives the Cost of Leveling a Mobile Home
sections.html:
No two homes settle the same way, so the price moves with a handful of factors. The big ones are the size of your home, how many piers need attention, and how far out of level it's drifted. A home that's a half inch off at one corner is a quick fix. A doublewide that's dropped two inches along the marriage line takes more jacks, more shims, and more time.

Here's what we look at when we build your quote:

  • Home size: A doublewide has roughly twice the piers of a singlewide, so full releveling costs more.
  • Severity of settling: Minor shimming is cheap. Sunken or cracked piers that need rebuilding add to the bill.
  • Soil conditions: Marion County's sandy soil drains well, but soft or washed-out spots may need extra footing work.
  • Access under the home: Tight crawl spaces, low clearance, or damaged skirting that has to come off slows the job down.
  • Add-on work: Torn vapor barriers, rusted straps, or missing anchors are often found once we're under there. We price those separately so you can decide.

sections.heading: Singlewide vs. Doublewide: Why the Price Gap
sections.html:
A singlewide relevel in our area runs $450 to $900. The crew works one beam line at a time, checks every pier with a water level, and shims until the whole frame reads true. Most singlewides are done in half a day.

A doublewide runs $700 to $1,500 because it's really two homes joined down the middle. Both sections have to come up together, and the marriage line has to stay aligned or you'll see it in sticking doors and drywall cracks. That takes more equipment and more careful sequencing, which is where the extra cost comes from. Homes in larger parks around Belleview and Summerfield are mostly doublewides, so budget toward the higher end if that's you.

sections.heading: Insurance, 4-Point Inspections, and Certification Letters
sections.html:
A lot of our calls start with an insurance letter, not a sagging floor. Florida carriers and lenders often want proof that a mobile home's tie-downs meet current code before they'll write or renew a policy. If your straps pass, a tie-down certification letter runs $150 to $300 and usually solves the problem the same week.

If the anchors are rusted out or there aren't enough of them, a full anchor and strap package runs $1,500 to $3,000 to bring the home up to code. That sounds like a lot until you compare it to losing coverage or a sale falling through. We keep a 24/7 line open for pre-closing deadlines because inspectors and underwriters don't wait, and neither do we.

sections.heading: How to Keep Your Leveling Costs Down
sections.html:
The cheapest relevel is the one you catch early. A corner that's an inch low today costs $300 to $600 to fix. Left alone for a few years, that same settling can crack piers, twist the frame, and pull plumbing joints apart, and now you're paying for repairs on top of leveling. If your doors have started sticking or you can feel a slope in the hallway, get it looked at now.

A few practical ways to save:

  • Bundle the work. If you need leveling and a vapor barrier, doing both in one visit costs less than two separate trips.
  • Fix drainage first. Gutters and grading that move water away from the home slow down future settling.
  • Get it in writing. Any quote worth trusting is a written one. Ours are free, and they're firm.
  • Recheck every few years. A $150 to $250 inspection is cheap insurance against a $1,500 surprise.

faq.q: How much does it cost to level a mobile home in Ocala?
faq.a: Most full relevels run $450 to $900 for a singlewide and $700 to $1,500 for a doublewide. A single settled corner is usually $300 to $600. Every job gets a free written estimate first, so you'll know the exact number before we start.

faq.q: How do I know if my mobile home needs leveling?
faq.a: The common signs are doors and windows that stick, cracks around door frames, soft or sloping floors, and gaps opening along the skirting. A $150 to $250 inspection will tell you exactly how far off level the home is and which piers need work.

faq.q: Does homeowners insurance cover mobile home leveling?
faq.a: Usually not for normal settling, since carriers treat it as maintenance. But insurance is often the reason leveling comes up, because Florida carriers frequently require a tie-down certification before writing or renewing a policy. That letter runs $150 to $300 if your anchors pass inspection.

Most singlewides take half a day and most doublewides take a full day. Bigger jobs that involve rebuilding piers or adding anchors can run into a second day. You can stay home while we work, since everything happens underneath.

faq.q: How often does a mobile home need to be releveled?
faq.a: In Central Florida's sandy soil, plan on a check every 3 to 5 years and a relevel somewhere in the 5 to 10 year range, depending on drainage and how the home was set. Homes with good gutters and grading go longer between visits.
